definitions.explanation: An official day off designated by the government.
A day on which a festival or celebration is held.

examples.japanese: {明日|あした}は{祭日|さいじつ}なので{会社|かいしゃ}は{休|やす}みだ。
examples.english: Tomorrow is a national holiday, so the company is closed.

examples.japanese: {日曜|にちよう}{祭日|さいじつ}は{営業|えいぎょう}していません。
examples.english: We are closed on Sundays and holidays.

examples.japanese: {祭日|さいじつ}には{旗|はた}を{掲|かか}げる{家|いえ}もある。
examples.english: Some households display flags on national holidays.

examples.japanese: {村|むら}の{祭日|さいじつ}にはお{祭|まつ}りがある。
examples.english: There is a festival on the village's festival day.

examples.japanese: {祭日|さいじつ}を{祝|いわ}って{町中|まちじゅう}に{飾|かざ}りがつけられた。
examples.english: Decorations were put up all over town to celebrate the festival day.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}では{秋|あき}の{祭日|さいじつ}になると、{毎年|まいとし}{伝統|でんとう}{的|てき}な{踊|おど}りが{披露|ひろう}される。
examples.english: In this area, traditional dances are performed every year on the autumn festival day.

notes:
{祭日|さいじつ} refers to national holidays or festival days.

TERMS FOR HOLIDAYS:
- {祭日|さいじつ}: holiday (older term)
- {祝日|しゅくじつ}: national holiday (official term)
- {休日|きゅうじつ}: day off, holiday
- {平日|へいじつ}: weekday

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {日曜|にちよう}{祭日|さいじつ}: Sundays and holidays
- {土日|どにち}{祝|しゅく}: weekends and holidays
- {祝|しゅく}{祭日|さいじつ}: public holidays

JAPANESE NATIONAL HOLIDAYS:
- {元日|がんじつ}: New Year's Day (Jan 1)
- {成人|せいじん}の{日|ひ}: Coming of Age Day
- {建国|けんこく}{記念|きねん}の{日|ひ}: National Foundation Day
- {春分|しゅんぶん}の{日|ひ}: Vernal Equinox Day
- {昭和|しょうわ}の{日|ひ}: Showa Day
- {憲法|けんぽう}{記念|きねん}{日|び}: Constitution Day

NOTE: {祝日|しゅくじつ} is more commonly used in modern Japanese than {祭日|さいじつ}.
